text:
Danila Yurov is the name in Minnesota's trade conversation. A Bolavip headline said the Wild reportedly included him in an offer for Detroit's Dylan Larkin and the Red Wings wanted more, and Hockey Wilderness has run pieces both for selling high and for taking him off the table.

The reason he's on the table: nine goals in 25 games at 22, already close to last season's 12 in 73. Five came in his last ten, including a two-goal game in Boston on Nov. 14. The process behind it is real. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 89th percentile for chances from the home-plate area last season, and his individual expected goals per 60 has climbed from 0.77 to 0.95.

But 23% shooting, against 15% last season, rarely lasts, and our numbers flag him to cool. Evolving-Hockey saw a defensive forward last season, with Minnesota creating little offense while he was out. Michael Russo of The Athletic noted he got dinged up in Boston and missed a practice; he has played every game since.
headline: Danila Yurov is scoring his way into trade talk
